controls.name: Input voltage
controls.high: 3.3 V gives 100%; out-of-range input is invalid.

lessons.concept: Variables hold typed values; functions separate calculation from I/O. Integer division loses fractional information. Always define units and valid ranges before coding.
lessons.contract: in[0] voltage in V, 0..3.3. out[0] percent, out[1] normalized ratio.

Calculate in floating point, retaining units.
Return percent and ratio separately.

lessons.concept: An array is a contiguous sequence. A pointer identifies an object, not its length. Structures group fields; enums name states. Here a checked array interface passes register and bit values to a pure function.
lessons.contract: in[0] bit 0..7 integer; in[1] register 0..255 integer. out[0] set result; out[1] clear result; out[2] mask.
algorithm: Validate index before shifting.
Create an unsigned one-bit mask.
Return set/clear results without changing other bits.
lessons.limits: No direct register access. volatile permits observable accesses; it does not provide atomicity or thread safety.
lessons.mutation: XOR toggles an already-set bit instead of preserving it.

lessons.concept: Little endian places the least significant byte first. Hexadecimal is only a representation, not a different quantity. A byte-order mismatch can produce plausible wrong values.
lessons.contract: in[0] unsigned integer 0..65535. out[0] low byte; out[1] high byte; out[2] reconstructed value.
algorithm: Check integer range.
Split into low and high bytes.
Recombine and compare with the original.

lessons.mutation: The high-byte shift is one bit too small.

lessons.opt: 10 ms for the demonstration; worst case is execution time greater than the period.
lessons.graph: Task releases must be equally spaced. A red deadline marker appears when simulated execution exceeds the selected period.
lessons.rig: One NUCLEO-G474RE through ST-LINK USB; no transceiver required.

controls.name: Task period
controls.low: 1 ms can overload a 2 ms task.
controls.nominal: 10 ms with 2 ms execution gives 20% utilization.
controls.high: 100 ms reduces load but makes control slower.

controls.name: Execution time
controls.nominal: 2 ms is illustrative, not measured MCU timing.
controls.high: Execution longer than period misses deadlines.

lessons.concept: Unsigned subtraction handles one timer rollover. Advance by complete periods to preserve phase, and bound catch-up work instead of running an unlimited burst. Processor timing must be measured separately.
lessons.contract: in[0] now, in[1] last: uint32 milliseconds; in[2] period 1..2147483647 ms. out[0] due flag; out[1] next release anchor; out[2] elapsed periods.
algorithm: Validate integer ranges and nonzero period.
Compute unsigned elapsed time.
Count completed periods and advance the phase anchor.
lessons.limits: Assumes elapsed time is less than 2^32 ms. Execution-time slider is a scheduling illustration, not timing measured from compiled code.
lessons.mutation: Rejecting wrap drops a valid release.
lessons.coverage: Graded core: in[0] now, in[1] last: uint32 milliseconds; in[2] period 1..2147483647 ms. out[0] due flag; out[1] next release anchor; out[2] elapsed periods. Other topics listed are theory or extension work, not additional simulated hardware.

controls.name: End terminators
controls.high: Two is correct; extra terminators overload the bus.

controls.name: Cable length
controls.nominal: 2 m at assumed 5 ns/m gives 10 ns one-way delay.
controls.high: 20 m gives 100 ns; this alone does not imply failure.

lessons.concept: The transceiver translates logic into differential signaling. Power rails are distinct nets. Termination is measured with all power removed. Missing termination is a wiring fault, but this ideal waveform model does not calculate cable reflections.
lessons.contract: in[0] terminator count 0..2; in[1] TXD 0/1; in[2] STBY 0/1. out[0] resistance ohm (-1=open); out[1] CANH V; out[2] CANL V; out[3] normal-transmit enabled.
algorithm: Validate discrete states.
Compute power-off parallel resistance.
Map dominant/recessive logic to illustrative bus levels.
lessons.limits: Voltages are typical teaching levels, not guaranteed datasheet limits. No signal integrity, ACK traffic or receiver thresholds are simulated here.
lessons.mutation: Using series instead of parallel resistance predicts 240 ohm.

controls.name: Node B identifier
controls.high: Equal IDs do not arbitrate further in this ID-only view.

lessons.concept: Both transmit MSB first. At the first different identifier bit, the node sending recessive but reading dominant loses arbitration and becomes a receiver. Losing arbitration is not a frame error.
lessons.contract: in[0], in[1]: standard IDs 0..2047. out[0] smaller ID; out[1] first different bit index 0..10, -1 if equal; out[2] winner 0=A, 1=B, 2=tie.
algorithm: Check 11-bit identifiers.
Compare bits from bit 10 down to bit 0.
Stop at the first difference and identify winner.
lessons.limits: ID field only; no bit stuffing, RTR/IDE arbitration, hardware CRC or TEC/REC simulation. Those remain theory and hardware-extension exercises.
lessons.mutation: Larger numeric ID is incorrectly selected.

controls.name: Frame valid
controls.low: Invalid frame enters DEGRADED unless already SAFE.
controls.high: Does not prove CRC/range by itself.

controls.name: Prior SAFE latch
controls.nominal: Reset only by deliberate recovery procedure.
controls.high: 1 remains SAFE even with fresh data.

equations: if prior SAFE or age>100: SAFE
else if invalid or age>30: DEGRADED; else RUN
lessons.concept: Only fully validated reception may refresh freshness. Unsafe payloads must not update application values. This kernel supervises an already-validated frame flag; parsing, CRC and counters belong before it.
lessons.contract: in[0] age ms>=0; in[1] valid 0/1; in[2] prior latch 0/1. out[0] state 0/1/2; out[1] next latch; out[2] output enabled (RUN only).
algorithm: Check inputs and prior latch.
Give SAFE precedence.
Enable output only in RUN.
lessons.limits: Qualification counters and controlled recovery are practice extensions, not silently claimed as implemented.
lessons.mutation: Ignoring the latch restarts outputs without authorized recovery.
